title: Choose the SageMaker inference contract before choosing compute
description: Select a workload and an inference mode. The lab checks documented request-shape boundaries and operating behavior; it does not invent latency, throughput, or price.

modes.label: Real-time endpoint
modes.detail: Persistent managed endpoint for sustained online low-latency or high-throughput traffic.

modes.label: Serverless inference
modes.detail: On-demand endpoint for intermittent traffic that can tolerate cold starts and service limits.

modes.label: Asynchronous inference
modes.detail: Queued endpoint for large payloads or long-running near-real-time work.

modes.label: Batch Transform
modes.detail: Finite offline datasets processed without a persistent endpoint.

scenarios.label: Checkout risk score
scenarios.detail: Sustained synchronous decisions on the user request path.

real-time.reason: The request is synchronous, small, and on a sustained low-latency path.
real-time.ownership: Autoscaling, model latency, capacity, and fallback

serverless.reason: The payload fits, but cold-start variance conflicts with this strict request-path objective.

async.reason: A queued result is incompatible with the synchronous checkout decision.
async.ownership: Queue delay, result polling, and expiry

batch.reason: The request arrives online rather than as a finite dataset.

scenarios.label: Large document extraction
scenarios.detail: Bursty 250 MB payloads can take fifteen minutes and callers can poll.

real-time.reason: The payload and processing time exceed the regular real-time request contract.

serverless.reason: The documented serverless payload and processing limits are too small for this request.

async.reason: The payload is below 1 GB, work is below one hour, and the caller accepts queued completion.
async.requestPath: Upload to S3, invoke asynchronously, read result from S3
async.ownership: Queue delay, notifications, retries, and result lifecycle

batch.reason: Batch also fits when documents are available as a finite offline dataset rather than arriving individually.
batch.requestPath: Transform job reads an S3 dataset
batch.ownership: Partitioning, job retries, and output reconciliation

scenarios.label: Nightly portfolio scoring
scenarios.detail: A complete dataset is ready before a fixed reporting deadline.

real-time.reason: A persistent request endpoint adds the wrong lifecycle for a finite offline dataset.

serverless.reason: This is dataset processing, not intermittent small synchronous requests.

async.reason: Individual queued requests are unnecessary when the complete dataset is known upfront.

batch.reason: Batch Transform is designed for large offline datasets without a persistent endpoint.
batch.requestPath: Transform job reads partitioned S3 input
batch.ownership: Deadline capacity, failed records, and output completeness

scenarios.label: Intermittent internal API
scenarios.detail: Small synchronous calls have long idle windows and tolerate measured cold starts.

real-time.reason: Real-time satisfies the request contract if paying for provisioned idle capacity is acceptable.

serverless.reason: Payload and processing fit documented limits, and the caller accepts measured cold starts.
serverless.ownership: Cold starts, concurrency, memory tier, and regional availability

async.reason: The caller requires a synchronous response and does not need a queued result.

batch.reason: Requests arrive individually rather than as a finite dataset.
